title: Dead Sea Mud Mask
body_html:
A pure dead sea mud mask for weekly detox, blackhead clearing, and deep pore minimizing — on your face, body, back, or anywhere excess oil accumulates. Three ingredients: Dead Sea Mud, Dead Sea Water, and a 1% organic preservative (Acribio OCS). No synthetic additives, no clay fillers, no harsh stripping agents. Just centuries-tested mineral therapy in a clean, vegan formula.

Key ingredients

  • Dead Sea Mud (Silt): Naturally concentrated with magnesium, calcium, and potassium — minerals that draw out impurities, calm inflammation, and tone the skin. The mud's negative charge attracts positively charged toxins and excess sebum, making it an effective natural clarifier without the harshness of acid-based treatments.
  • Dead Sea Water: Carries the same mineral profile in soluble form, reinforcing the mask's conditioning and calming effects on the skin barrier as it detoxes.
  • Acribio OCS (1% organic preservative): The only non-mineral additive — a COSMOS-approved organic preservative used to ensure microbial safety in a water-based formula. One percent. That's it.

What it does

  • Draws out blackheads and excess oil: The adsorptive properties of Dead Sea silt pull congestion from pores without stripping the skin's natural moisture.
  • Minimizes pore appearance: Regular weekly use visibly tightens and clarifies pores over time, particularly effective on oily T-zones, backs, and chests.
  • Calms and tones: Magnesium and potassium from the mineral-rich mud have a calming, anti-inflammatory effect — this is why Dead Sea therapy has been studied for conditions like psoriasis and eczema.
  • Detoxes without over-stripping: Unlike acid peels or aggressive clay masks, this mud detoxes gently — the mineral balance means skin feels clean and smooth, not tight or irritated.

How to use

  1. Apply a thin, even layer to clean, dry skin — face, back, chest, or other oil-prone areas. Avoid the eye and lip area.
  2. Leave on 10–12 minutes, or until fully dry.
  3. Remove with warm water using gentle circular motions to lift the mud and any loosened impurities.
  4. Pat dry and follow with your regular moisturizer.
  5. Use once a week (up to twice weekly for oily skin). Do not use daily — over-masking disrupts the skin barrier even with a gentle formula.

Routine pairing

Use as a weekly ritual alongside your daily routine — not instead of it. On mask days: cleanse, apply Dead Sea Mud Mask, remove after 10–12 minutes, then continue your normal routine (serums, moisturizer, SPF if AM). Your daily actives — Vitamin C Serum, Vitamin Glow Serum, or PDRN Brightening Serum — work best on skin that's been regularly cleared of congestion. The mask handles the deep-pore work; your daily serums handle tone, hydration, and brightening.

Who it's for

For moms who want a clean, no-nonsense skin detox without acids, harsh astringents, or a long ingredient list to decode. Ideal for oily or combination skin types, anyone with regular congestion or blackheads, and those who want a face-and-body option that's genuinely clean. If you're into EWG-style label transparency, this ingredient list is about as honest as it gets: three ingredients, all accounted for.

Free from

No parabens • No sulfates • No synthetic fragrance • No PEGs • No phthalates • No artificial additives

Full ingredient list

Dead Sea Mud (Silt), Dead Sea Water, Acribio OCS (1% organic preservative)

Suggested Use: Apply a thin, even layer to clean skin, avoiding the eye and lip area. Leave on 10–12 minutes or until dry. Remove with warm water using gentle circular motions. Pat dry. Use twice weekly, followed by your favorite moisturizer.

Warning: For external use only. Avoid contact with eyes. Discontinue use if irritation occurs. Keep out of reach of children. Not for use on broken or irritated skin. Store in a cool, dry place.

7 oz (198g) · Made in USA

faq_json.question: How often should I use this?
faq_json.answer: Once a week is the sweet spot for most skin types. If you have oily or congested skin, you can use it up to twice a week — but no more. Even a gentle, mineral-based mud mask draws out oils and tightens pores, and over-masking (more than twice weekly) can start to disrupt your skin barrier and trigger rebound oil production. Think of it as a weekly ritual, not a daily step.

faq_json.question: Is it safe for sensitive skin?
faq_json.answer: Dead Sea minerals are actually known for their calming and anti-inflammatory properties — this is part of why Dead Sea therapy has been studied for psoriasis and eczema. The formula has only three ingredients, none of them synthetic irritants. That said, everyone's skin is different. If you have highly reactive or broken skin, do a patch test first (inner arm, 24 hours) and avoid applying to areas of active irritation. Because this formula uses 1% Acribio OCS as a preservative, those with known preservative sensitivities should review that ingredient before use.

faq_json.question: Can I use it on my body too?
faq_json.answer: Yes — this was formulated for face and body. It's particularly effective on the back, chest, and shoulders where blackheads and congested pores are common. Apply the same way: thin, even layer, 10–12 minutes, rinse with warm water. The 7 oz jar makes this practical for larger body areas in a way a typical 1 oz facial serum isn't.

faq_json.question: What's the difference between this and clay masks?
faq_json.answer: Both draw out impurities, but the mechanisms and mineral profiles differ. Standard clay masks (kaolin, bentonite) rely on clay's absorptive properties and are essentially mineral silicates. Dead Sea mud is a distinct geological material — it contains a richer profile of biologically active minerals (magnesium, calcium, potassium, sodium) in higher concentrations than most clays, along with organic matter from the Dead Sea basin. Dead Sea mud also tends to be less drying than bentonite, which can over-strip. The calming, anti-inflammatory mineral content is where Dead Sea mud stands apart.

faq_json.question: Is it safe during pregnancy?
faq_json.answer: The three ingredients here — Dead Sea Mud, Dead Sea Water, and a 1% organic preservative — are free from the actives most commonly flagged during pregnancy: no retinoids, no high-dose salicylic acid, no hydroquinone, no synthetic fragrance. Dead Sea mineral therapy is generally considered low-risk. As always, we recommend checking with your OB or midwife before adding any new skincare product during pregnancy or breastfeeding — they know your individual health picture and can give you personalized guidance.

faq_json.question: How do I apply and remove it?
faq_json.answer: Apply a thin, even layer to clean, dry skin — face, back, chest, or any oil-prone area. Avoid the eye area and lips. Leave on 10–12 minutes, or until the mud has fully dried (it will lighten in color as it dries). Remove with warm water and gentle circular motions — the motion helps lift loosened debris from pores. Pat dry, then apply moisturizer. Avoid using hot water to remove, which can over-strip the skin post-mask.

faq_json.question: Will it dry out my skin?
faq_json.answer: No — not when used as directed. The 'mud equals harsh stripping' assumption usually comes from experience with high-percentage bentonite clay masks, which can be over-drying. Dead Sea mud has a different mineral composition and a gentler drying effect. The Dead Sea Water in this formula also contributes a mineral-conditioning element as the mask dries. Used once a week (or max twice for oily skin), the detox effect is clarifying, not dehydrating. Follow with a moisturizer after rinsing and your skin should feel clean and smooth — not tight.
